issues.legal_issue: A firm’s status as an agriculturist for purposes of a restriction on purchasing agricultural land depends on the activities of its partners, including their personal cultivation, and not on the firm being an inanimate entity.
material_facts: A firm purchased agricultural land at an execution auction.
The partners comprising the firm were found to be agriculturists.
The objection to the auction sale was brought in execution proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to treat the firm as incapable of being an agriculturist merely because the firm itself was inanimate; its status depended on the activities of its partners, who personally cultivated land.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(2) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, an agriculturist is a person who cultivates land personally. A firm is a collective name for its partners, who are natural persons, so the partners’ activities determine whether the firm is an agriculturist. The issue of the partners’ status was referred for determination by the revenue court under Section 85-A of that Act.

issues.definition: When an objection to an auction sale is considered in execution proceedings, a purchasing firm whose partners personally cultivate land is treated as an agriculturist.

issues.legal_issue: An auction purchase of agricultural land is void when it causes the purchaser’s joint-family holding to exceed the applicable ceiling.
material_facts: The firm’s partners were members of a joint family whose landholding was already reckoned as a joint-family holding.
The auction purchase increased that holding beyond the applicable ceiling.
The judgment-debtor’s heirs objected to the auction sale in execution proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The auction sale was void, the objection was sustained, and the Executing Court’s order as affirmed by the First Appellate Court was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 63 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, prohibits any person, including a Hindu joint family, from purchasing land if the purchase would cause the holding to exceed the applicable ceiling. The restriction applies to an auction purchase, and a sale that contravenes it is void. The objection was pursued under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
